set.st: Brewer Joseph Ritter stored forty barrels of beer in a cellar dug 30 ft into a hillside about the 1860s; the tunnel caved in. After the brewery was razed, owner Charles Ney let four young men sink a shaft (AP, 14 May, 1920s). On 23 May 1926 five Henderson men (Mimbach, Whelan, Teschendorf, Beecher and Hensler) said the dig had stalled, that it might take a steam shovel and dynamite, and that they were looking for a backer. By 7 Nov the casks were up and in litigation: the county attorney called them wet contraband, and an heir in St Paul claimed a share. The dates: in Oct 1925 the UP reported two huge oak casks buried about 60 years earlier in a hillside tunnel at Joseph Ritter's brewery, after Charles Ney razed the brewery that summer; in May 1926 four men were digging 30 ft down with a chart from old brewery employees, and the Volstead officers were asked for a ruling. In May 1926 a digging party at 'the ruins of the old Ritter brewery' was halted by heavy masonry, and old-timers doubted the casks were there.
set.y: stored c.1865; dug May 1926; raised 7 Nov (1926, year to confirm)
